characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Suns universal testing machine with Reliant electronic extensometer
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast exhibited YS = 772.3 MPa, TS = 879.0 MPa, EL = 20.53% and Z = 17.10% (Table 2); its stress–strain curve plateaus between 800 and 900 MPa and ends just past 20% strain, lower in strength and plasticity than the SLM-printed samples (Fig. 12).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: loading rate 1 mm/min; dog-bone-shaped specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm; room temperature
characterization_methods.purpose: to evaluate the room-temperature tensile properties (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation) of the as-cast Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy for comparison with SLM-printed samples

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: tensile strength and plasticity (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: As-cast Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy used solely as the control/benchmark state against the SLM-printed samples for tensile property comparison (Table 2, Fig. 12). The paper does not report any specific casting process details (melt temperature, mold material, cooling conditions) for this sample; it is only described as the conventional 'as-cast' condition.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: loading rate 1 mm/min; Suns universal testing machine with Reliant electronic extensometer
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile sample, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: As-cast (orange) engineering stress–strain curve: steep elastic rise then a plateau between 800 and 900 MPa, terminating just past 20% strain (Fig. 12).

unmapped_findings: The as-cast Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni sample's reduction of area (Z) = 17.10% is reported in Table 2 (and Fig. 14(c)) but has no dedicated slot in the tensile_properties schema (which covers yield strength, tensile strength and elongation).

The as-cast sample is the weakest of the compared conditions: its tensile strength (879.0 MPa) is well below all SLM samples, and its elongation (20.53%) and reduction of area (17.10%) are the lowest of the group (Table 2, Fig. 12).

No microstructural (XRD/EBSD/TEM/OM), density, hardness, porosity or surface-roughness characterization is reported in the paper for the as-cast sample; all such data concern the SLM-printed samples only.
